name: inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-pulp-timer-zipdma-4w-compressed-control-f1-fuzz
notes: trigger_writes and status_offsets repeat the values already used by configs/scenarios/inprocess-irq-pulp-timer-profile.json; the entry re-checks them against the timer register map and interrupt declarations
dma_window must not overlap the APB target window; the timer owns 0x40000000..0x40000fff
the timer declares 50 MHz, the CPU 50 MHz and the ZipDMA a nominal 1 Hz simulation rate, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives all three models

f1_program_words 4 declares a four-record-word compressed image and f1_allow_compressed_control widens the admitted parcel set with C.J/C.JAL/C.JR/C.JALR/C.BEQZ/C.BNEZ.  Every target must be a strictly forward instruction start of the image (or the appended return jump); C.JR/C.JALR are admitted only when their base register is statically proven to hold one exact constant address, and C.JR x0 is a reserved encoding.  A backward compressed transfer would be a loop and is refused by name, as are the FP/stack-pointer/RV64 forms.  The retirement evidence is the parcel/word RVFI trace: prog_retires counts instructions, prog_trace_hash (FNV-1a 32 over pc/insn/rd/wdata with the 16-bit parcel as insn) is compared with the Python reference trace.  Evidence: runs/round1-f1-controlflow/.

fuzz_flows ["F1"] narrows the closed-loop batch to the F1 program flow, so every generated and mutated input is a program of the declared shape whose RVFI retirement trace is compared with the Python reference trace.  The same host/timer/DMA models are built; only the offered flow set changes.
